description: Hand-maintained performance groupings for cases the heuristics in dataset/canonical/performance_groups.py cannot settle. Each entry of `groups` unions the listed IDTAP transcription ids (the `_id` field) into a single performance group, on top of the automatic shared-audioID and (soloist, raga, title) rules. Ids that do not exist in the fetched transcription list are ignored with a warning, so a stale override never breaks a build. Every group must carry a human-readable `reason` stating the evidence, because these merges are not reproducible from the data alone.

fields.recording_ids: list of IDTAP transcription `_id` values to union (2 or more)
fields.reason: why these are one performance; cite durations, audio ids, or external knowledge
fields.added_on: ISO date the override was added
fields.confidence: one of high | medium | low, the annotator's own assessment

groups.reason: D.V. Paluskar, Bhopali/Bhup, under three different audioIDs (64fedda02f5f4d9c1b63648c, 65b149747f607fb149202017, 65b14c577f607fb149202018) so the shared-audio rule cannot see them, and three different titles ('D.V. Paluskar - Bhopali', '... Bhopali Vilambit', '... Bhopali, Jab Se Tumi Sab Laagali') so the title rule cannot either. Durations give it away: 1119.5 s + 575.2 s = 1694.7 s against the single 1691.1 s transcription, a 3.6 s difference. Almost certainly one performance uploaded once whole and once split into vilambit and bandish halves. Grouped deliberately: if the guess is wrong we lose a little split granularity, if it is right and we do not group we leak the same audio across train and test.
